info.name: Care Companion - System Prompt
info.description:
The system prompt the assistant runs on, and the documents behind it.

Update overwrites the prompt body and APPENDS files. Delete removes one document from S3 and Mongo and leaves the others standing.

The database is the only source of the prompt - nothing is shipped on disk. Until a prompt is stored, GET returns an empty `system_prompt` and the chat endpoint answers 503.

Set the `baseUrl` variable to your server. `fileId` is filled in automatically by the Update and Get requests, so Delete is ready to send.

exec: // Remember the first document so the Delete request is ready to send.

formdata.value:
## 1. WHO YOU ARE

You are the Care Companion team's secure automated AI assistant...
formdata.description: The prompt body. Overwrites whatever is stored, and is the assistant's only instructions - keep the '## 6. REVIEWED WORDING' section or the reviewed emergency and consent wording stops being substituted. Leave this row disabled to add files without touching the prompt.

What the chatbot is called. It is passed to the assistant as its own name, so it answers 'What is your name?' with it - the prompt text does not need to mention it. Left out, it keeps the stored name; a prompt-only update does not clear it.
REQUIRED. The tenant's ObjectId, stored exactly as sent - nothing is derived or padded. It must be a real 24-character ObjectId; anything else answers 400.
Pick one or more .docx, .txt or .md files. Their text is extracted and appended to the prompt as approved documents; the file itself goes to S3.

request.description:
One tenant's record. `tenant_id` is required and says whose prompt is being written; send a prompt, a chatbot name, files, or any mix alongside it. An update carrying none of those is rejected with 400.

Each field is independent: one you leave out keeps that tenant's stored value. Files are APPENDED to that tenant's documents.

Nothing is written until every file has been read and stored, so a refused file type or an unreachable bucket leaves the record untouched.

exec: pm.test('answers for the tenant asked for',

query.description: REQUIRED. The tenant's ObjectId, stored exactly as sent - nothing is derived or padded. It must be a real 24-character ObjectId; anything else answers 400.

request.description:
That tenant's prompt, chatbot name, and only its documents. Each document carries a presigned `url` that expires after S3_URL_TTL seconds.

`tenant_id` is required and must be a real 24-character ObjectId; it is stored and returned exactly as sent.

A tenant with nothing stored answers 200 with an empty `system_prompt` and no files.

Removes that one document from S3 and from Mongo. Every other document stays.

`fileId` is set for you by the Update and Get requests; you can also paste any id from their `result.files[].id`. An unknown id answers 404.

request.description:
`tenant_id` is required and decides everything the assistant answers with: that tenant's prompt, its chatbot name, and only its documents. Another tenant's documents are never read.

A tenant with no stored prompt answers 503 rather than falling back to anyone else's.

Needs OPENAI_API_KEY set.
